items.title: Chuck Findley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 6, 2023
items.q: I was on the road for the summer of ’65 with the Jimmy Dorsey band

ctx.x: Before I leave your childhood I just wondered what it was like to be making some money and going to high school or middle school, wherever you were. Did you stand out as a student like man, he’s playing gigs? © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

You know actually yes. That’s true. When I was in middle school or junior high we called it then, junior high school. I was doing these, like I said I was doing these gigs and playing these and then making some money, not a lot of money but it was some cash you know. But I knew that I wanted to be a trumpet player already. I knew that because my brother was — jeez when I was 14 my brother was 22. He had already been on the road with the Ray McKinley band, the Glenn Miller band. He went out with Ralph Marterie’s…
I was trying to come up with a description of that and it almost sounds like someone writes a book, “Chuck Makes Good,” and it’s all like fantastic.
